summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening nausea, vomiting, and a severe migraine, along with hypoxia on exertion. She also reported persistent right-sided chest and clavicular pain following a recent fall. Evaluation showed no evidence of peritonitis or pneumonia; chest imaging revealed atelectasis likely due to splinting from pain. Her symptoms were attributed to a migraine flare with associated gastroparesis, and her hypoxia resolved with supportive care. She received IV anti-nausea medication, migraine treatment, and overnight peritoneal dialysis. An irrigation of the peritoneal cavity was performed. Her condition improved, she tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to follow up for pain and vaginal itching, and a prescription for fluconazole.
